title: Discovering Significant Patterns under Sequential False Discovery Control

problem.claim: Discover patterns whose empirical frequency differs significantly from what is expected.

gap.claim: Pattern search must avoid spurious results and redundancy while retaining high statistical power and efficiently handling an exponentially sized search space.

contributions.claim: A method called Spass sequentially controls false discoveries during pattern search.
The method updates expectations when a significant pattern is discovered to avoid redundancy.
The method uses an easy-to-compute upper bound on significance and a search strategy for sets of significant patterns.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On synthetic data, the authors report that Spass reliably recovers the ground truth, operates efficiently, and avoids redundancy.
On real-world data, the authors report that Spass works well across single and multiple classes and across low- and high-dimensional data.
The authors report that case studies using Spass discover meaningful results.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper targets discovery of patterns whose empirical frequency differs significantly from expectation.
It proposes sequential false-discovery control during search to reduce spurious results while maintaining statistical power.
It updates expectations after discovering significant patterns to reduce redundancy.
It uses an upper bound on significance and a search strategy to handle the exponentially sized search space.
Experiments on synthetic and real-world data report reliable, efficient, nonredundant, broadly applicable, and meaningful results.

source_observation.claim: Updating expectations after discovering significant patterns is presented as a way to avoid redundancy.

interpretation.claim: Sequentially revising the search reference point may reduce repeated or overlapping discoveries.

application.claim: In sequential discovery workflows, consider updating expectations after each accepted significant result.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when expectation updates are appropriate or how they affect different pattern spaces.

source_observation.claim: The method combines an upper bound on significance with a search strategy for an exponentially sized search space.

interpretation.claim: Search efficiency can be improved by pruning candidates using inexpensive significance bounds.

application.claim: For large combinatorial searches, evaluate whether computable upper bounds can guide candidate pruning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish the bound's tightness or its performance outside the reported settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal false-discovery control procedure or guarantees.
The abstract does not report quantitative experimental results, baselines, or computational costs.
The abstract does not define the pattern class, significance test, or data assumptions.
